transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Start time: 10:00 UTC
Duration: ~63 minutes
Attendees: Sanjay, Maya, Noah, Liam, Evelyn, Zara, Ava + company-wide (approx 150 attendees on call)

---
[00:00] Sanjay Rao: Hey everyone, thanks for joining our October all-hands, appreciate folks dialing in from APAC late. Quick housekeeping — we'll run about an hour, save Qs for the end, but feel free to drop them in chat.

[01:12] Sanjay Rao: Quick high-level — Q3 closed strong, revenue up vs plan, a few big Dedicated deals pushed us over the quarter target, and Private pilots are picking up. Maya, quick on infra?

[02:05] Maya Patel: Yep, thanks. Engineering shipped two major runtime optimizations this month — improved KV cache eviction and a new batching heuristic that reduces tail latency on mixed workloads. We're seeing 15-20% p95 improvements in internal tests, and cost per token is down for long-context jobs. Caveat, some edge cases with very short sequences saw slight overhead, we're rolling a toggle.

[04:30] Noah Kim: To add, the kernel selector now prefers quantized-friendly paths for most 16-bit->8-bit profiles; that's helped on A100s and the newer Ampere-family cards. We'll surface a benchmark sheet after the call. Sorry if I said "Ampere" wrong earlier in a doc, transcription had that weirdly as 'ampere family' — you know how the export is.

[06:10] Liam O'Connor: On product — shipped first pass of the caching API and the Optimize suggestions UI. The Optimize engine now recommends batching sizes per route; it suggests per-route quantization for customers that want cost reductions. Reminder: these are suggestions, not auto-enforced changes.

[07:40] Evelyn Park: From GTM: three net-new Dedicated contracts closed in Q3, two of them are mid-market SaaS companies moving from self-hosting to Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency. We also have a large enterprise security review ongoing with a regulated fintech — privacy, KMS, and audit logs were the main asks. Sales will need the SOC2 artifact for the next meeting.

[09:25] Zara Hassan: Customer success — pilot health looks good, churn is low among customers who enabled prefix caching. We did have one pilot where latency regressions happened after a private deploy; engineering rolled a quick patch. We'll send a root cause note.

[11:02] Sanjay Rao: Quick finances — burn is within plan, runway 15 months at current pace, revenue beats helped. We're continuing disciplined hiring but hiring where it matters: infra, SEs, and account execs. People Ops to give numbers?

[12:10] Ava Martinez: Hiring update — we're at ~150 headcount today, plan to end year ~165. Priorities: two senior infra engineers, three SEs, one senior product manager. Referral bonus reminder in HR channel.

[14:00] Anonymous Question (chat): will we open an office in Berlin?

[14:12] Sanjay Rao: Short answer — exploring EMEA presence, nothing firm yet. Partner channel might be first step.

[15:30] Maya Patel: Security update — SOC2 Type II audit kickoff next month, plus we've added rotation for KMS keys on the private control plane. For Private customers we now support customer-managed HSM integrations in the lab. Docs will be uploaded to the security portal.

[17:05] Liam O'Connor: Roadmap high-level for Q4: 1) GA of caching API and per-route suggestions, 2) rollout of canary A/B rollouts in Console, 3) expanded model catalog with two new LLaMA-derivative models tuned for conversational safety, 4) Dedicated autoscaling improvements.

[19:40] Noah Kim: Technical note — the autoscaler will support 'burst capacity' settings so Dedicated pools can temporarily exceed baseline for short workloads; we'll add guardrails to avoid cost shocks. There was an internal ticket where an autoscale misconfig caused excessive provisioning last month, we fixed it and added alerts.

[21:55] Evelyn Park: On partners — closed a reseller arrangement with a managed hosting partner in Japan, helps our APAC reach. Also evaluating cloud marketplace listings; expect to start listing Dedicated in at least two clouds by early 2027.

[24:30] Sanjay Rao: Hiring/comp — we will publish a Q4 compensation refresh update next week, nothing dramatic, just adjustments to keep market competitive.

[26:05] Zara Hassan: Customer stories — highlight a mid-market SaaS that reduced inference cost by ~30% moving to our batching + quantization suggestions; we'll draft a short case study.

[28:20] Audience Q (voice): Is the Optimize suggestions engine safe to run in prod?

[28:45] Liam O'Connor: Good Q. It's designed to be advisory only; you opt-in for automatic application. We have guardrails and a dry-run mode so you can see predicted savings without changing live config.

[30:00] Audience Q: Any changes to data retention policy for hosted API?

[30:20] Maya Patel: No policy changes today — retention defaults unchanged. For enterprise customers we continue to offer configurable retention and purge pipelines; SSO and RBAC improvements coming.

[32:05] Sanjay Rao: OKRs — top company OKRs for Q4: 1) 99.95% platform uptime, 2) 20% reduction in avg per-token cost for top 10 customers via Optimize, 3) 3 GA partner integrations for Dedicated, 4) close $X ARR in Reserved capacity contracts (internal target). Managers to cascade to teams.

[34:40] Anonymous (speaker 7): A little noisy on my side — sorry if I misspeaking — is the model catalog expanding open models or proprietary?

[35:00] Liam O'Connor: Primarily curated open models and variants we test — tuned variants will be Redwood-verified but remain open-model based. Some customers ask for custom tuning; we'll support that via Dedicated or Private.

[36:20] Noah Kim: Ops note — new tracing hooks in console to help debug KV cache misses and prefix cache effectiveness. The UI may be rough at first; SEs will have training sessions.

[38:05] Evelyn Park: Sales enablement — updated battlecards for Dedicated vs Hosted, and competitor notes (Anthropic/OpenAI comparisons). Please review and provide feedback in the sales channel.

[40:00] Q&A rapid fire: People ask about international pricing, docs for on-prem install, and pilot timelines. Answers: pricing review underway, docs link posted after call, pilot onboarding checklist to be compiled by CS.

[44:10] Sanjay Rao: A few shoutouts — infra team moved fast on the caching fix, sales team closed tough deals, and CS kept pilots healthy during ramp. Thanks everyone.

[46:00] Audience Question: Any updates on research into attention/kernel optimizations?

[46:25] Maya Patel: Team is exploring better fused attention kernels; some promising leads from community OSS patches. We'll evaluate impact on latency and memory. No release dates yet.

[48:10] Short break in audio — transcription shows garbled words here, something like 'k v catch' turned into 'k v ketch' in the export.

[50:00] Sanjay Rao: Closing remarks — momentum is good, Q4 is about execution. Focus on reliability and helping customers adopt Optimize recommendations safely. We'll follow up with the Q4 plan doc.

[51:30] Open mic (20 min): lots of small team updates and shoutouts; can't capture all — refer to #all-hands thread.

[63:00] End
